title: Passport
body_markdown:
## What is Passport?

Passport refers to a vast archive of national and local content that users have access to when they have donated a specific amount to their PBS station.

## How does Passport work?

- When a user donates to your station, an activation code is generated and sent to the user.
- The user enters the activation code when signing on to the video portal.
- MVault communicates to the video portal that the user has access to Passport content.
- The user is welcomed to Passport and has access to premium content.
- MVault records that the user has activated the database is synced.

[Check out what this process looks like to your users](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505084).

title: Membership Vault
body_markdown:
Membership Vault (MVault) is a membership registry that enables stations to provide members conditional access to premium PBS digital features.

Are you a Developer? [Go to the MVault developer documentation](https://docs.pbs.org/space/MV/5799938/Membership+Vault+(Passport)+Developer+Documentation).

- [Overview](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505026/Membership+Vault#Overview)
- [Requirements](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505026/Membership+Vault#Requirements)
- [Membership Vault Dashboard](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505026/Membership+Vault#Membership-Vault-Dashboard)

## Overview

Membership Vault (MVault) is a membership registry system that enables stations to provide conditional access to premium PBS digital features. Through MVault, stations can manage the relationships between its members and online offers, and acts as a gatekeeper (essentially determine thumbs-up or thumbs-down access per member) for online digital services. For example, a service such as Passport queries MVault to determine if a viewer is allowed access. MVault makes it easy for stations to adopt new offerings without additional work.

- Membership has its privileges. MVault provides premium PBS digital offerings to your qualified members. This is a huge benefit as more and more people are choosing to consume content online.
- Explore new avenues for expanding your membership base. MVault helps you tap into and stay connected to your online audience. As the digital ecosystem continues to evolve, viewers are using various donation methods to support their local station.
- Easy set-up. Even if your technical resources are limited or non-existent, MVault is designed to be fully operational and easy to integrate with your existing membership management system.

## Requirements

To use MVault, you must have a PBS Account. [Learn how to get a PBS Account](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505080/How+to+Create+a+PBS+Account).

## Membership Vault Dashboard

The [MVault Dashboard](https://mvault.console.pbs.org/admin/) serves as a quick reference guide for station-specific membership information. Each icon represents a filter that, when clicked, displays results for the corresponding category. For instance, if you click Activated, only the memberships that have activated display. [Access the MVault console](https://mvault.console.pbs.org/admin/).

| Category | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Total | Total number of your station's membership records, regardless of offer access eligibility. |
| Recently Added | Membership records created in the last seven days. |
| Provisional | Members flagged for station approval. Provisional status does not affect offer access. Useful for making sure payments have gone through. You can go back and change the status if payment was rejected. If using bulk import such as Allegiance, you don't really need to use this feature. |
| Activated | Members who have completed the activation process. |
| Currently Active | Members with offer access, based on: 1) Activation Date is populated; 2) Status=On; and 3) Today's date falls within the Start and Expire dates. Note: This does not include members within Grace Period. |
| Expiring Soon | Memberships that will expire within the next 30 days. |
| Grace Period | Members within the 90-day Grace Period, following their Expire Date. |
| Expired | Memberships that have passed the Expire Date. |
| Possible Duplicates | Multiple memberships with matching email addresses. MVault duplicates may occur when the station's donation form logic and/or CRM/Integration logic are not updating existing MVault records, but rather creating a new MVault record for the member for each renewal. |
| Possible Temporary Membership IDs | This is useful for stations using the PBS donation form, which generates new MVault records using “temp-id” as the temporary Membership ID prefix. |
| Recent activity | A current list of the most recent activity in your station's Membership Vault account. |
| History/Expiring Memberships | All recent activity in your station's Membership Vault account. All memberships that are about to expire. |
| All History | A record of the all activity in your station's Membership Vault account. |

title: Getting Help
body_markdown:
MVault offers an array of options to help you out as you navigate the console. The Help section can be accessed from all pages of the console and you do not need to be logged in to view it.

- On every page of the console, in the left side navigation menu, click Help (Figure 1).
- In the Help section, click FAQ to access common questions and answers related to MVault (Figure 2.1).
- Click Documentation to review user guides and related MVault information (Figure 2.2).
- Click Community to access community forums where you can share ideas, view recent announcements, and find tips and tricks (Figure 2.3).
- If your question is not answered through the FAQ, Documentation, or Community links, click Contact Support to [submit a ticket](https://digitalsupport.pbs.org/support/tickets/new) for help (Figure 2.4).

title: MVault Console
body_markdown:
## Overview

After you've [created a PBS Account](https://docs.pbs.org/x/4U0F), log in to the [MVault console](https://mvault.console.pbs.org/) to manage the relationships between your members and online offers.

## The console

After logging in, you are automatically directed to your station dashboard and your login displays in the far upper left side of the screen.

- If you have access to more than one station, click the station dropdown menu in the upper right corner of the page and click the station you want to view (Figure 1.1). If you have access to just one station, this option is not available.
- A status summary of all members displays in a menu at the top of the page (Figure 1.2). Click an icon to go to the All Members view.
- The most recent activity history displays (Figure 1.3).
- Click the Expiring Membership tab to view memberships that are close to expiring (Figure 1.4).
- Click the All History at the bottom of the table to view all History (Figure 1.5).
- Use the menu links on the left side of the page to navigate to other areas of the console (Figure 1.6).
- Click the left-facing arrow to expand the view of the main content area (Figure 1.7).

title: FAQ
body_markdown:
## Is the email address that a user activated Passport with the same email address on record in MVault?

Not necessarily. A user can activate using any email address they like. While we would prefer they use the same email address as what is in MVault, it is not guaranteed.

## Should we have individual logins for MVault or one that we all share?

You can do either. Different permissions can be assigned to different logins, so if you have users who should not have extensive access to the tool, they can be assigned one shared login, while those who dig down a little more into the tool's features can have wider permissions assigned to their login.

## I need access to the MVault console but I don't have a PBS Account. What can I do?

As part of your station onboarding process, begin by [requesting access](https://digitalsupport.pbs.org/support/tickets/new) to the MVault console. When you receive an email invite to access the console, you will be prompted to log in or [create a PBS Account](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505080/How+to+Create+a+PBS+Account).

## Is there a way to see a summary of my MVault activity?

Yes. The Membership Vault console homepage displays a dashboard with a summary of your member information, as well as a list of the most recent actions taken in your MVault account. [Learn more](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505026/Membership+Vault#Membership-Vault-Dashboard).

## If I use a program such as Allegiance for my donation form, will members be automatically added and activated?

Yes.

## Can I delete a member?

Yes. Users can be deleted from within the console or via the API. If you think a member may be renewed in the future, you can prevent the user access to the station offer in one of the following ways:

1. Set the member's Status to Off
2. Change the Expire Date to a date in the past.

[Learn more about deleting from the console](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505101/Memberships#How-to-delete-a-membership-record)

## Can I delete an offer?

Yes, but only if that offer is not assigned to any membership records. In this case, deletion is prevented. [Learn more about deleting offers](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505072/Offers#How-to-delete-an-offer).

## Can I deactivate a member?

Yes. To prevent access to the station offer for a member, you can either:

1. Set Status to Off
2. Change the Expire Date to a date in the past.

Since deleting a member is permanent, we recommend deactivating a member if the membership may be renewed in the future.

## What should I do with updated credit card information for my donors?

When a donor makes a monthly donation on the Passport page, they are processed as a sustainer (monthly recurring donation does not expire).

If a member contacts you with updated credit card information, you should process them as a sustainer on your end and then file a ticket (via the Digital Support Portal) to let us know that we should cancel the recurring payment for the old/bad credit card in our system.

## Is the Membership ID generated by MVault?

No. The station assigns the Membership ID, and it should correspond with the ID used for the member in their CRM/database. The User Profile ID, however, is assigned by MVault after a member has completed the activation process. This is internal to PBS and is not editable.

## Do I need to calculate and add a Grace Period to a member's Expire Date?

No. The 90-day Grace Period is automatically calculated within MVault when a station admin selects or changes (and saves) the Expire Date. The Expire Date will not be changed. Instead, you will see a read-only field within the console (or API), which provides the Grace Period end date.

## Is a member considered "active" while within Grace Period?

No. Users within the Grace Period will have Passport access for 90 days after their Expire Date, but they are considered expired and not active.

## Can a user activate while within their Grace Period?

Yes.

## How do I get member activation tokens?

There are three options:

1. If you just need activation tokens for a few members, you can look up the individual membership records within the [console](https://mvault.console.pbs.org/admin/) and grab the tokens.
2. Use the Export feature within the console to download a CSV file of membership records with activation tokens. You can download all records or select a date range based on record creation.
3. Use the [MVault API](https://docs.pbs.org/space/MV/5799969/Membership+Vault+API) to retrieve membership records with activation tokens.

## What does "Provisional" mean?

MVault was designed to be a permissive system, which enables new members to get immediate access to your station's offer. The Provisional setting allows stations to keep track of new members for whom they have not yet confirmed that the donation requirement has been met.

Example: A user donates to their station over the phone, and mails a check. The station creates a membership record for the new user and allows them to activate immediately, trusting that the check will arrive and clear. By setting this member as Provisional, the station can keep track of them until they have been fully verified. Once the station determines that the check has cleared and the donation requirement was met, they can update the field so the member is no longer Provisional.

Notes about the Provisional setting:

- The setting does not affect a member's ability to access the station offer (such as Passport).
- It is not exposed to members, meaning they will not know if they are Provisional or not. Only stations see this setting.
- It is a purely administrative field, intended to help stations keep track of unverified, new members.
- When creating individual memberships within the console (by clicking "Create Membership" button), Provisional is assigned by default.
- When viewing an individual membership record within the console, the values for Provisional are: Yes/No
- When using the CSV Import method, or the MVault API, the values for Provisional are: true/false
- It is recommended that all new members are set to Provisional, until the station determines the donation requirement has been met – at which time the setting can be updated.

## What does "Status" mean?

Think of it as an emergency cut-off (but not a cut-on) switch.

When Status=Off:

- Prevents the member from having access to the station offer (such as Passport) – in all cases.
- Provides a quick way for stations to shut off access, without having to alter the Expire Date field.

When Status=On:

- Allows the member to have access to the station offer (such as Passport), if the following criteria is also met:
  - The member has completed the activation process. You can determine this by looking at the "Activation Date" field. If it's empty, they have not completed activation.
  - The membership is within the Start and Expire Dates – or within Grace Period, which is 90 days following the Expire Date.
  - If criteria #1 AND #2 are not met, the member will not have access to the station offer, even if Status=On.

## The member's "Status" is "On" but the member does not have access. What gives?

The Status field is just one of three criteria that must be met, in order for a member to have access to the station offer (such as Passport).

A member will have offer access if:

1. Status=On
2. The member has completed the activation process. You can determine this by looking at the "Activation Date" field. If it's empty, they have not completed activation.
3. The membership is within the Start and Expire Dates – or within Grace Period, which is 90 days following the Expire Date.

If criteria #1, #2, AND #3 are not met (all three), the member will not have access to the station offer, even if Status=On.

Sidenote: If Status=Off, this prevents access to the station offer regardless of any additional criteria. (See FAQ for: What does "Status" mean?)

## What is considered "Recently Added"?

A "recently added" member is a new member who was added to MVault in the last seven (7) days.

## What is considered "Activated"?

An "Activated" member is a member who has fully completed the [Passport activation process](https://help.pbs.org/support/solutions/articles/5000693823-what-does-the-activation-process-look-like-).

## What is considered a "Currently Active" member?

Currently Active reflects the number of membership records considered “active” and members who currently have access to the offer (Passport). This means all membership records where:

1. The Activation Date is populated (user is activated);
2. Status=On;
3. Today’s date is between the Start and Expire dates for a user.

All three criteria must be met. Currently Active excludes members within Grace Period.

## What are "Possible Duplicates"?

Possible Duplicates refers to instances where there are multiple records with the same email address.

## When is a membership considered "Expiring Soon?"

Memberships that are expiring soon will expire in 30 days or less.

## My station uses Team Approach. Is there an automated option available for MVault integration?

Yes! Team Approach has developed a method to integrate your CRM with MVault, and operationalize the management going forward. It's called Team Approach Passport Synchronization (TAPS), and the documentation/scripts are included here:

[Download file Team Approach Passport Synchronization.docx](https://docs.pbs.org/rest/api/content/5505078/child/attachment/att5506028/download)

[Download file scripts-121715.zip](https://docs.pbs.org/rest/api/content/5505078/child/attachment/att5506092/download)

## I don't see an answer to my question here. Where can I get more help?

For additional help, click [Help](https://mvault.console.pbs.org/admin/help/) located in the left side navigation menu in the console.

title: How to Create a PBS Account
body_markdown:
## Overview

This page is intended for anyone who needs to create a PBS Account to access PBS Digital tools such as Bento, Media Manager, etc. If you would like instructions on how to create a PBS Account to log in to [PBS.org](https://pbs.org/), please [view the PBS.org help pages](https://help.pbs.org/support/solutions/articles/12000086698-how-do-i-create-a-pbs-account-).

## What is a PBS account?

PBS Account is a login system that allows you to maintain a single identity across PBS products. When you create a PBS Account, your login and password moves between each product to which you've requested access.

This section shows you how to create a PBS account if you do not currently have one, and how to navigate your account information once you have logged in.

Stations can request access to PBS Digital Platforms such as MVault, Bento, Media Manager, Curate, etc. by submitting a ticket at [http://digitalsupport.pbs.org/support/tickets/new](http://digitalsupport.pbs.org/support/tickets/new).

## How to create a PBS account

- Go to the product URL and click Login. The product URL is the link to the product console. View a list of available consoles on the [docs.pbs.org homepage](https://docs.pbs.org/) under PBS Digital Consoles.
- Click Create an account (Figure 1).
- In the textboxes provided, type your first name, last name, email address, and password (Figure 2.1). Your password must contain at least eight (8) characters, with a combination of letters and numbers.
- Click Create an Account (Figure 2.2).
- You are redirected to a confirmation screen indicating that your login is successful (Figure 3). After a few seconds you are automatically redirected to the console homepage.
- You are logged in and your name displays in the upper right side of the page.

## Next steps

Stations can request access to PBS Digital Platforms such as MVault, Bento, Media Manager, Curate, etc. by submitting a ticket at [http://digitalsupport.pbs.org/support/tickets/new](http://digitalsupport.pbs.org/support/tickets/new).

## How to sign in

If you already have a PBS Account, follow the instructions below to sign in using your PBS Account.

- Go to the console dashboard and click the login button or link.
- In the Email Address textbox, type the email address that is associated with your PBS Account (Figure 1.1). This is the email address you used when you created your PBS Account.
- In the Password textbox, type the password that is associated with your PBS Account (Figure 1.2). Click Show Password to display the password as you type.
- Click Sign in with Email (Figure 1.3).
  - If you do not have a PBS Account, click Create an account to create one (Figure 1.4).
- After you have successfully signed in, a screen stating that your login is successful displays (Figure 2).
- After a few seconds, the screen automatically redirects to the console homepage and your login displays in the upper right side of the page.

## How to log out

In the upper right corner of the console, click your name and click Log out.

## How to delete your account

This section is for users of [PBS.org](https://pbs.org/). After you've created a PBS Account, you can delete it at any time. Deleting your account does not affect your Passport membership or any recurring donations that you have scheduled. To cancel your membership, please contact your local station. If you want to associate your Passport account with another email address, use the [Passport reset feature](https://pbs.org/passport/reset/).

This section shows you how to delete your PBS Account.

- After logging into the site, click your name in the upper right corner (Figure 1.1).
- When the menu displays, click Profile (Figure 1.2).
- Click Privacy Settings (Figure 2).
- Click the red Delete Your Account button (Figure 3).
- When the confirmation modal displays, click OK (Figure 4).
- A screen confirming the deletion has been successful displays (Figure 5). You are no longer able to sign in to [PBS.org](https://pbs.org/) with that email address.

Your account information has been deleted from PBS Account but your Passport membership is still active and any recurring donations you have in place will continue.

Close the browser window and return to the PBS website. The PBS site might show that you are still signed in, but after clicking anything on the site you will no longer be logged in. After deleting your account, you can create a new PBS Account with a different email address or, if you've changed your mind, the email address that was just deleted.

## How to change your password

This section shows you how to change your PBS Account password.

- After logging into the site, click your name in the upper right corner (Figure 1.1).
- When the menu displays, click Profile (Figure 1.2).
- Scroll down the page and click the Account Security section (Figure 2).
- Click the pencil icon to the right of Password (Figure 3).
- In the Password textbox, type your current password (Figure 4.1).
- In the New Password and Re-enter New Password textboxes, type your new password (Figure 4.2).
- Click Save Changes (Figure 4.3).
- A confirmation message displays, indicating that your password has been reset (Figure 5.1).
- Click Back to Profile to return to your main profile screen (Figure 5.2).

## How to create a strong password

- Use a pass phrase that is easy for you to remember, but hard for someone to guess.
- Avoid obvious patterns such as qwerty, abcdef, ggghhh, 123321.
- Avoid stand-alone words, in any language, including slang or jargon, followed by a digit and/or symbol. Example: Password1$.
- Avoid using your name, or the names of family members or pets, SSN, phone numbers, etc.
- Avoid writing down your password, or storing your password on any system without encryption.
- Avoid sharing your password with anyone.
- Do not use the same password for work and personal accounts.
- Your password must be treated as confidential information.

A password might meet all the criteria above and still be a weak password. For example, Hello2U! meets all the criteria for a strong password listed above, but is still weak because it contains a complete word. H3ll0 2 U! is a stronger alternative because it replaces some of the letters in the complete word with numbers and also includes spaces.

Tips for remembering your password:

- Create an acronym from an easy-to-remember piece of information.
- Substitute numbers and symbols for letters and words in an easy-to-remember phrase. Example: Pick a phrase that is meaningful to you, such as “I love winter”. Using that phrase as your guide, you might use 1l0v3w1nT3r for your password.

If you feel you must write down your password in order to remember it, make sure you don't label it as your password, and keep it in a safe place.

| Term | Definition | Example | Notes |

| Activation Date | The date that the member activates their account on pbs.org. | 2014-09-11 12:03:00 | Is generated once the member activates their account on video.pbs.org. This cannot be modified. |

| Grace Period | An automatically generated date that extends a member’s access to Passport content for 90 days after their expire date. Members have Passport access but are not considered "active" during the grace period. The grace period is automatically generated in the console and API and cannot be changed. | Nov. 16, 2016, 1:06 p.m. EST | Times are eastern standard time. | Possible Duplicates | Members with matching email addresses. May be generated when using bulk import using an external program such as Allegiance. | | |
| Possible Temp IDs | Members who have a temporary temp ID. Generated when a station uses the PBS donation form. A temporary ID is automatically generated and a station must go back update the IDs with the station's generated IDs. | | |
| Provisional | A designation indicating whether or not the user donation has made its way completely through the system or if it is still processing | Yes | Provisional is set to Yes for all new membership records. It’s up to the station to switch it to No when they determine a user has met the donation requirements. |
| Recent Activity | Located at the bottom of your dashboard, this is a record of all recent activity in your station's MVault account. | | |
| Start Date | The time and date the membership is activated. | 2014-09-22 13:17:55 | |
| Status | Indicator for whether the membership is active or not. | ON | |
| User Profile ID | Auto-generated unique identifier of the user who activates the membership. | | This does not appear in the member record until the user has completed the entire login process on video.pbs.org. Once created it cannot be modified. |

title: Offers
body_markdown:
## What is an offer?

An offer is a feature set conferred upon users who have donated a specific amount to their PBS station. Currently, PBS offers Passport, an online video feature which gives members access to a vast archive of national and local content.

## How to create an offer

Once an offer has been created, it cannot be deleted.

- From the left side navigation menu, click Offers (Figure 1).
- Click Create Offer located on the right side of the page (Figure 2).
- In the Title textbox, type the name of your offer (Figure 3.1). Use names that clearly indicate the offer. Be clear and concise. This is a required field.
- The Offer ID automatically generates when the page is saved. You can leave this field blank (Figure 3.2).
- In the Description textbox, type a brief description of the offer you are creating (Figure 3.3). This is not a required field but is helpful to offer context to what is being offered. Other people who use the console should know what each offer entails.
- When finished, click Create (Figure 3.4).
- The offer is saved and has been assigned a Created and Last modified date (Figure 4.1). Each time this offer is modified, the Last modified date changes to reflect the date of the change.
- Click Offers on the left side navigation menu to view all offers (Figure 4.2).

## How to edit an offer

You can make changes to an offer at any time.

- From the left side navigation menu, click Offers to access all of your offers (Figure 1.1).
- Click the title of the offer or the pencil icon to the right of the offer that you want to modify (Figure 1).
- Click each textbox to make modifications (Figure 2.1).
- When finished, click Save (Figure 2.2).
- Click Offers to return to the main Offers page (Figure 2.3).

## How to delete an offer

Only offers that are not assigned to a member can be deleted.

- From the left side navigation menu, click Offers (Figure 1.1).
- To delete from the Offers dashboard, click the trashcan icon from the Actions column (Figure 1.2) or click the offer Title to open the offer and delete from there (Figure 1.3).
- When prompted to confirm the deletion, click Yes, I'm sure (Figure 3).
- A confirmation stating that the offer has been deleted displays in green at the top of the screen (Figure 3).

A deleted offer cannot be recovered, only recreated.

## How to view offer history

Offer history provides a record of what has been changed and who has made the changes to existing offers. View the history for all offers or for an individual offer.

### View all offers

- From the main Offers screen (Figure 1.1), click the History button located in the upper right side of the screen (Figure 1.2).
- Click the filters located on the right side of the page to drill down and view a specific action, offer, or user. As you click each filter, the list of offer records in the center of the screen automatically refresh to reflect your selections. Action = the action that was taken on the offer. Offer = select a specific offer to view actions on only that offer. User = search for a specific user who has taken actions on offers in the database.
- Click the records per page dropdown to select the number of record results you wish to view on one page.
- Type search criteria in the textbox to search results. All columns can be searched.
- Date reflects the date and time an action was taken on the offer.
- User is the person taking an action on a membership record.
- The Offer column displays the name of the offer.
- The Offer ID is the unique identifier for the offer.
- Station reflects the station to which the offer is attached.
- The Action column displays the actions taken on a specific offer.
- The Details column provides more information on the action that was taken on the offer.

### View an individual offer

- From the main Offers page, click the offer whose history you want to view (Figure 1).
- Click the History button located in the upper right side of the screen (Figure 2).
- All of the actions that have been taken on that specific offer display (Figure 3).

title: Search
body_markdown:
## Overview

Use the search feature in MVault to perform detailed searches on a variety of fields and return specific records. Instead of exporting all membership records and sorting in an Excel file, use the MVault search to retrieve just the records you want and then [export just those results](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505113/Search#How-to-export-results). This page shows you how to search for a record using one parameter or build a detailed search based on several parameters.

## Fields that can be searched

| Field | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| First Name | Member's first name |
| Last Name | Member's last name |
| Email | Member's email address on file |
| Phone | Member's phone number on file |
| Offer | The name of the offer associated with the membership |
| Membership ID | A unique identifier generated for the membership |
| Start Date | The time and date the membership is activated |
| Expire Date | The time and date the membership expires and the member can no longer access offers |
| Create Date | The date the membership was created |
| Update Date | The date the membership was updated |
| Activation Date | The date that the member activates their account on [pbs.org](https://pbs.org/) |
| Grace Period End Date | Automatically generated date that extends a member’s access to Passport content for 90 days after their expire date |
| Provisional | Designation indicating if the user donation has made its way completely through the system or still processing |
| Status | Indicator for whether the membership is active or not |
| User Profile ID | Auto-generated unique identifier of the user who activates the membership |
| MVault ID | Auto-generated unique ID associated with the member record. Can be used to associate TVault information. |
| Creator | |

## Search modifiers

The search form has a variety of ways to modify your search to narrow down the results. Each form field has a unique set of modifiers that are used. This section provides an overview and definition of each modifier.

### Member information

First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Membership ID, User Profile ID, MVault ID, Creator

| Modifier | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Equal | Search value is equal to the exact text specified |
| Not Equal | Search value is not equal to. Results exclude specified values |
| Begins with | Results begin with text being searched |
| Doesn't begin with | Results do not contain specified text |
| In | Text should be included in results |
| Not In | Results should not contain text |
| Contains | Record contains text |
| Doesn't contain | Record does not contain text |
| Ends with | Record ends with text |
| Doesn't end with | Record does not end with text |
| Is empty | Field is empty in record |
| Is not empty | Field is not empty in record |

### Dates

Offer, Start Date, Expire Date, Create Date, Update Date, Activation Date, Grace Period End Date

| Modifier | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Equal | Search value is equal to exact date or offer that is being searched |
| Not Equal | Search value is not equal to search criteria. Results exclude search value. |
| Greater | Value is greater or later than specified value. If a date, results are later than the value specified in your search. |
| Greater or Equal | Value is greater/equal or later/on the same date as specified value |
| Less | Value is lesser or before specified value. If a date, results are dates earlier than the date specified in your search. |
| Less or Equal | Value is lesser/equal or earlier/on the same date as specified value |
| Between | Value falls between two dates |

### Member account status

Provisional

| Modifier | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Yes/No | Is the member's status provisional |

### Member activation status

Status

| Modifier | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Off/On | Is the member's status active |

## How to search

The search feature offers several filters to help you find specific records. Review the [fields that can be searched](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505113/Search#Fields-that-can-be-searched) and the [modifiers](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505113/Search#Search-modifiers) that can be used to drill down to a particular record. This section illustrates how to use the search feature with one search parameter. [Learn how to build a search using multiple search parameters](https://docs.pbs.org/space/PLUS/5505113/Search#How-to-build-a-search).

- Access the search feature by clicking Memberships on the left side navigation and expanding the section (Figure 1.1).
- Click Search (Figure 1.2).
- The search feature displays (Figure 1.3).
- Click ADD RULE (Figure 2.1).
- Click the dropdown box that displays on the left side of the page (Figure 2.2).
- Click the filter on which you want to search (Figure 2.3).
- Type the filter you wish to search on in the box on the right side (Figure 3.1).
- Click the filter menu (Figure 3.2).
- When the list of modifiers displays, click the search modifier you want to use (Figure 3.3).
- When you've finished selecting all the filters you want to search on, click Apply Filters to initiate the search (Figure 4).
- All results related to the filter display (Figure 5.1). Click Open Column Chooser to select which columns you wish to display in the results table (Figure 5.2).

## How to build a search

Retrieve a specific MVault record or set of records by building a search using a combination of rules and groups. Use the groups feature to nest queries and drill down to a specific set of records.

Part of building a search is using the AND/OR command, which determines if the search results match all search criteria or some.

- AND - Search results should match all of the search criteria
- OR - Search results matches any of the search criteria

## How to customize results table

Use the Column Chooser to determine which fields should display in the table. Field names with a checkmark beside them display in the table and fields without a checkmark are hidden. This section shows you how to use the column chooser to display only the fields you wish to view.

- Directly above the results table, click Column Chooser (Figure 1).
- Click the checkbox next to the fields you wish to display. Fields that do not display a checkmark do not display in the results table. In the example below (Figure 1), only the following fields will display in the results table: First Name, Last Name, Status.
- The selected fields display in the results table (Figure 3).

## How to export results

After generating your search results, export them to a CSV file with the Export feature.

- When your search results are ready, click Export located above the search results table on the right side of the page (Figure 1).

## How to clear rules

There are a couple of different ways to clear search rules:

- Click the Delete button next to each filter you want to remove from your search (Figure 1.1).
- Click Reset to remove all filters (Figure 1.2).

## How to reset the results table

After you've conducted a search and the results display in the table, click the Reset button to go back to the default table view.

## How to reset table sorting

To clear your filters and return to the default table view, use the Remove Sort option available on any column that has been sorted.

- Click the menu icon in each column that has been sorted (Figure 1.1).
- Click Remove Sort (Figure 1.2).

After clicking Remove Sort in each column that has been sorted, the table goes back to its original state and is void of all sorting and filters.
headings: How to reset the results table
